methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multicenter cohort study (n=136) across 3 Portuguese institutions (2007-2021). Clear inclusion/exclusion criteria; post-pubertal males with histologically confirmed TGCT. Stratified analysis by disease stage (early stage n=99 vs. advanced/recurrent n=37). Statistical methods: univariate logistic regression for TE predictors (due to small events n=7); univariate Cox for survival (binomial approach due to insufficient multivariable power). Appropriate given event rarity. Khorana and ONKOTEV scores validated despite lack of predictive performance. Long follow-up (median 58.2 months early stage, >5 years advanced).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort (LoE 2b) characterizing TE risk in TGCT population undergoing cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Directly relevant to young cancer patients where thromboembolism is under-recognized complication (~10% in advanced TGCT). Key finding: TE only in advanced disease (5.1% overall, 14.6% advanced) with no benefit from current risk scores (Khorana, ONKOTEV failed prediction). Highlights need for TGCT-specific prophylaxis tools. Clear clinical implications for supportive care.

reporting_quality.justification: Follows STROBE principles: study design clear, baseline characteristics reported (Table 1), inclusion/exclusion explicit, outcome definitions standardized (RECIST 1.1, Lugano criteria for imaging response). IRB approval documented, waiver of consent justified. However, no data repository or sharing plan. Missing: detailed TE event descriptions (number, anatomic sites, timing relative to cycles), follow-up imaging protocols across centers, complete baseline laboratory values for logistic regression.

novelty_literature.justification: Study characterizes real-world TE incidence in TGCT (5.1% overall, 14.6% advanced stage) consistent with prior reports (~10% in advanced TGCT). Novel aspects: Portuguese real-world data, explicit validation that Khorana (recommended in ESMO guidelines) and ONKOTEV scores do NOT predict TE in TGCT despite good performance in other cancers. Highlights disease-specific risk factors (bulky retroperitoneal nodes, visceral metastases, CVC use) but lacks mechanistic insight. Incremental contribution to TGCT-specific risk stratification.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written introduction contextualizing TGCT curability and TE as underappreciated morbidity. Methods clearly describe study design, patient selection, statistical approach (with transparent acknowledgment of univariate-only analysis due to small event numbers). Results organized by stage cohorts. Key finding (Khorana/ONKOTEV failure) emphasized appropriately. Discussion compares to prior Spanish cohort data and ESMO guidelines. Some density in baseline data could be streamlined; effective communication of main message.

key_strengths: Addresses important supportive care gap: TE is under-recognized complication in young TGCT patients with potential for life-threatening morbidity
Clear stratification finding: TE occurred exclusively in advanced/recurrent disease (5.1% overall, 14.6% advanced); no TE in stage I despite adjuvant chemotherapy (n=22 treated)
Explicit validation that current risk prediction tools (Khorana ≥3, ONKOTEV ≥4) failed to predict TE, supporting need for TGCT-specific risk model
Identified risk factors: visceral metastases (pulmonary, extra-pulmonary) and poor IGCCCG prognosis associated with TE; all TE patients had central venous catheters (p=0.019 difference)
Long-term follow-up with survival outcome data showing TE did not significantly impact OS (71.4% vs. 86.2%, p=0.22) or PFS (47.6% vs. 75.5%, p=0.23)
key_concerns: Very small TE event sample (n=7/136, 5.1%) limits statistical power; univariate analysis only, multivariable regression not feasible due to overfitting risk
Retrospective design with potential surveillance bias: TE detection may depend on clinical presentation severity; asymptomatic DVT may be under-ascertained
Missing mechanistic insights: why cisplatin-induced TE occurs only with advanced disease unclear; no laboratory markers (platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen) reported for TE cohort
CVC not universally documented across centers; unclear if 'all TE patients had CVC' represents true finding or ascertainment bias (CVC more likely placed in advanced patients)

Survival outcomes not significantly different between TE and non-TE groups despite clinical concern; potentially underpowered or suggests TE not independent prognostic factor in highly curable disease
No external validation; single Portuguese multicenter cohort; generalizability to non-European TGCT populations unclear
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid real-world characterization of TE complication in TGCT addressing important supportive care question, but small event numbers and retrospective design limit causal inference. Appropriate for Tier 4 (descriptive epidemiologic cohort). Accept as correctly-conducted study highlighting clinical need for TGCT-specific TE risk tools and prospective validation studies.
